proposed_from.topic:
Flat-strip completion of the thickness-multiplicity frontier for boundary causal traces. This is a new attempt at banked parent stat_bdd_thickness_estimability_frontier, not a retry of its circular annulus witness. Observe iid O=(X,T,Y), X=(R,S) in [-1,1]^2, T=1{R>=0}, on B={(0,s):|s|<=1/2}; target the contrast of unique bounded L-Lipschitz observed-side traces under conditionally sigma-sub-Gaussian errors. For q_t(x,h)=P{X in side t and B_2(x,h)}, impose common lower mass c_m h^kappa. Let J_P(h,u) be the h-packing number of boundary sites with min_t q_t(x,h)<=u. Define isolated laws by one threshold-thin site plus J_P(h,u)<=C_iso{1+h^-1(u/h^2)^(1/(kappa-2))}, and pervasive laws by J_P(h,C_m h^kappa)>=c_J/h. Prove explicit normalized Cartesian product/radial-power laws and Gaussian tent alternatives make both classes nonempty. Prove matched expected-sup risks n^-1/(kappa+2) and (log n/n)^1/(kappa+2), one kappa-free count estimator attaining the pervasive/base rate, and an explicit finite-pattern band with finite-sample simultaneous coverage over every declared nonempty triangular profile union and matching pervasive all-band expected-width lower bound. Do not use circular coordinates, unit-circle packing, the parent's vacuous side-mass placeholder, or claim arbitrary-profile/local-oracle band exactness. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Writing alpha=kappa-2, the flat pervasive density normalizes as (kappa-1)|r|^alpha/4, while the clipped radial-power law has explicit normalizer 4-V_alpha/(alpha+2). Cartesian rectangles and half-balls give uniform one-sided h^kappa masses, including both segment endpoints, and imply the full isolated J_P envelope. Severity-layer peeling yields the isolated no-log upper bound; deterministic boundary grids, finite-pattern calibration, and Gaussian tents give the pervasive lower and band routes. At kappa=3 the pervasive tent product KL is nL^2h^5/(480 sigma^2). Checks covered 78 mass configurations, large-radius clipping, u=1, asymmetric sides, empty counts, and endpoint geometry; constants are uniform only on compact exponent sets bounded away from 2, and the observed-side regressions themselves remain L-Lipschitz. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently formalize the combined normalized flat witness membership and tent-validity theorem, including Borel laws, support, conditional kernels, all mass/profile inequalities, target separations, and Gaussian product KL with the declared target segment. EARLY KILL TEST: Verify the draft's equations (2.1)-(2.6) and construct the actual observed Gaussian laws for both endpoints, clipped radii, u=1, and the smallest admitted exponent; stop if any membership inequality must be assumed. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_bdd_flatstrip_thickness_entropy_frontier.md.

D-1 SCOPE AUDIT (controlling accepted scope): The exploratory topic above proposed matched lower bounds and a finite-pattern simultaneous-confidence-band/width program. Across D-1 revision, the accepted kernel was explicitly narrowed to the total global-bandwidth profile-adaptive estimator and its isolated, pervasive, and regular expected-sup risk conclusions. The confidence-band/width program was withdrawn and is not delivered here; no finite selector, packing event, or anchor construction is a confidence band. Exact endpoint lower bounds, if restated, are attributed supporting converses from the banked parent rather than a new novelty claim. The note’s novelty is simultaneous cross-regime attainment by the present estimator.
proposed_from.novelty_justification: Gaiffas (2007) adapts at one degenerate-design point, whereas the distinct Gaiffas (2009) uniform paper uses location-specific normalization for finitely many one-dimensional zeros. Boundary-discontinuity theory studies a causal curve on a continuous-score-density class bounded away from zero. The first nontrivial result here, and the sole closed novelty claim, is the packing-oracle inequality for one total measurable estimator whose empirical penalty learns the number of comparably thin boundary sites. Its attributed endpoint corollary records same-estimator isolated/pervasive upper-rate adaptation under polynomial two-sided depletion without re-claiming the banked minimax lower bounds. The explicit finite selector and event-explicit remainder close the measurability gap without changing the field-tier kernel, while the packing-comparison lemma ensures uniform calibration does not reinstate the global logarithm removed in the isolated regime.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Gaiffas's Theorem 1 and equations (2.4)--(2.5) derive the single-point bias--information rate from a regularly varying design, while its proof localizes Gaussian alternatives at one design zero. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu's Introduction, Assumption 1(ii), and sharp-BATEC convergence theorem treat an entire bivariate assignment boundary but require the score density to be bounded away from zero. Their extensions section leaves poorly supported boundary regions outside the stable local-polynomial theory.
seed_details.kernel: Construct normalized Cartesian laws that realize isolated and pervasive sets of polynomially thin boundary sites, then prove the matched expected-sup risk frontier, a \(\kappa\)-free count estimator, and an honest finite-pattern band with a matching pervasive width lower bound.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the one-point regularly varying neighborhood integral and the positive-density boundary Gram bound by exact one-sided rectangle and half-ball masses, followed by severity-layer packing rather than a global union bound.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches combining boundary discontinuity curves, polynomially vanishing one-sided score mass, thin-site packing multiplicity, minimax supremum risk, and honest bands found no theorem at this intersection.
adjacent_threads: Gaiffas2007UniformInhomogeneous: finitely many one-dimensional zeros and spatial normalization
CattaneoTitiunikYu2026DistanceBoundary: boundary minimax theory under positive density
ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands: uniform calibration under regular studentization
seed_details.red_team: Immediate from Gaiffas because a boundary segment is only a continuum of degenerate design points.
seed_details.rebuttal: Gaiffas fixes one zero or finitely many zeros and uses spatial normalization; it does not compare same-modulus classes whose number of worst sites changes the unweighted expected-sup rate, nor certify two-sided causal traces and simultaneous-band width.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The kernel is a same-class upper-and-lower frontier over explicit nondegenerate law classes, not a single witness or a routine positive-density dimensional extension.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Gaiffas's Theorems 1--2 characterize pointwise risk through the smallest solution of a bias--local-information equation for regularly varying and \(\Gamma\)-varying designs. The construction remains one-point and does not contain a boundary packing functional.
seed_details.kernel: Give an if-and-only-if oracle functional for expected-sup boundary-trace risk under an arbitrary two-sided tube-mass modulus and compatible lower and upper thin-site packing profiles, including polynomial and exponential corollaries.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace regular-variation inversion of one local information equation by a multiscale infimum balancing bias, local mass, and realizable packing entropy at every severity layer.
seed_details.target_method_search: The search found spatially inhomogeneous normalization in Gaiffas but no same-class modulus--packing characterization for causal boundary traces.
adjacent_threads: AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014DensityZeros: global risk with finitely many density zeros
CattaneoTitiunikYu2025BoundaryRD: causal boundary curve under positive density
seed_details.red_team: The proposed oracle is merely the maximum of Gaiffas's pointwise rates with an inserted entropy term.
seed_details.rebuttal: That objection fails only if compatibility conditions are shown necessary and sufficient and the upper profile and lower realizable packing generate the same functional; this unresolved equivalence is the theorem-level content.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed requires both directions and explicit realizability; a one-sided bracket would be rejected.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Bull's Introduction and Theorems on adaptive bands show that self-similarity is essentially necessary for smoothness adaptation, using confidence-band-to-testing reductions. Armstrong and Kolesar's Introduction and least-favorable convex testing construction give finite-sample scalar modulus bounds and bias-aware intervals, but not a boundary-indexed thickness-profile criterion.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize a necessary and sufficient full-observed-law separation condition under which one honest band adapts its expected width between isolated and pervasive thickness profiles.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace separation between smoothness classes by testing between score-and-outcome profile unions, and replace a scalar modulus by a location-indexed conditional calibration.
seed_details.target_method_search: Searches found smoothness self-similarity and scalar RD modulus theory, but no necessary-and-sufficient adaptation condition indexed by the multiplicity of thin boundary sites.
adjacent_threads: Bull2012HonestAdaptiveBands: necessary self-similarity for smoothness adaptation
seed_details.red_team: Bull's self-similarity theorem already supplies the needed adaptation criterion after relabeling smoothness as thickness.
seed_details.rebuttal: Thickness is a random-design information profile rather than a property of regression coefficients; equal score marginals can still have distinguishable outcome kernels, so the relevant full-law testing geometry is different.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The exact iff boundary and a constructive band are required; sufficient-only adaptation is not counted.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu define side-specific local-polynomial Gram matrices after Assumption 1 and derive their convergence and uniform inference under positive score density and regular boundary geometry. Their setup makes coercivity load-bearing but does not characterize it under vanishing mass.
seed_details.kernel: Give primitive flat-strip density and radial-balance conditions that are sufficient, and near-necessary through explicit singular counterexamples, for uniform signed-distance local-polynomial Gram coercivity at polynomially thin sites.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the positive-density rescaling limit of each Gram matrix by a quantitative subannulus moment bound and identify the first radius concentration pattern that makes polynomial columns collinear.
seed_details.target_method_search: The boundary local-polynomial literature states geometric and eigenvalue regularity, while manifold local regression links support geometry to conditioning; no sharp flat-strip mass-versus-Gram frontier was found.
adjacent_threads: CattaneoTitiunikYu2026DistanceBoundary: signed-distance geometry and positive-density minimax theory
Gaiffas2005DegenerateDesignRates: local polynomial normal equations under a design zero
seed_details.red_team: Standard cone conditions automatically imply the desired eigenvalue bound.
seed_details.rebuttal: Cone support alone does not control radial concentration when density vanishes; the result must quantify radial balance and exhibit scalar-mass laws with singular higher-order moments.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim includes a necessity boundary and a nondegenerate counterexample region rather than an abstract sufficient eigenvalue assumption.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Armstrong and Kolesar characterize optimal confidence intervals for linear regression functionals over convex classes through least-favorable pairs. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu define weighted boundary averages and derive regular positive-density local-polynomial inference.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a semiparametric efficiency bound for a weighted boundary trace average under polynomial score depletion and construct an attaining estimator.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Test pathwise differentiability of the boundary integral when the transverse score density vanishes, before attempting an influence-function calculation.
seed_details.target_method_search: The search found regular-density weighted boundary inference and nonregular scalar modulus theory, but no root-\(n\) efficiency calculation under polynomial depletion.
seed_details.red_team: The boundary trace is nonregular, so a finite semiparametric efficiency bound and root-\(n\) attaining estimator generally do not exist.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds for the declared Lipschitz class without extra smoothing of the target; imposing such smoothing would change the estimand, so this lane is dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The M11(b) lane was tested first and rejected at pathwise differentiability rather than being replaced by another rate claim.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato's Introduction and Theorems 2.1 and 3.1 replace a required extreme-value limit by Gaussian anti-concentration and multiplier calibration. Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu use boundary-indexed Gaussian approximation under a score density bounded away from zero.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the uniform weak limit, or prove the absence of a universal limit and give a valid conditional approximation, for the studentized count-selected boundary-trace supremum under the pervasive polynomial flat law.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace uniform variance stabilization under positive density by self-normalization with random polynomially sparse disk counts before applying Gaussian coupling.
seed_details.target_method_search: No limit theorem for a count-selected boundary process with vanishing transverse density was found; existing generic bands assume nondegenerate studentization.
adjacent_threads: Bull2012HonestAdaptiveBands: data-selected resolution and band behavior
seed_details.red_team: Generic Gaussian approximation already covers this VC-indexed disk process.
seed_details.rebuttal: At the thinnest scale the studentizing counts are random and near the admissibility threshold, so nondegeneracy and anti-concentration must be re-established rather than imported.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The limit or conditional approximation is the headline, not an accessory to a matched-rate theorem.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Cattaneo, Titiunik, and Yu motivate heterogeneity of the BATEC along the eligibility boundary and define weighted and largest boundary effects, but their identified effects concern marginal units on the boundary.
seed_details.kernel: Learn a constrained treatment rule along the boundary with regret governed by the thin-site packing profile.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Translate boundary trace estimates into a policy value and verify that the policy's counterfactual welfare is identified for the population on which it acts.
seed_details.target_method_search: Policy-learning papers require an identified value for deployable assignments; the boundary design identifies only local effects for marginal score values.
seed_details.red_team: A rule that changes treatment away from the assignment boundary has an unidentified value under continuity-based regression discontinuity assumptions.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds in the declared model, and restricting the policy to a measure-zero boundary has no population welfare content; this lane is dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The M16 lane was not padded with an unidentified welfare target.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato obtain honest bands through Gaussian approximation and multiplier calibration, not exact permutation symmetry; their construction tolerates data-selected resolution under regular studentization.
seed_details.kernel: Invert sign or permutation statistics to obtain an exact finite-sample band for the boundary trace under polynomial thinning.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Identify a group action leaving the centered outcome law invariant conditional on the scores.
seed_details.target_method_search: The declared model assumes only conditional sub-Gaussian residuals, which need not be symmetric or exchangeable under sign flips.
seed_details.red_team: There is no exact symmetry orbit under the stated error model, so permutation inversion cannot guarantee coverage.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds unless Gaussian or symmetric errors are imposed as a stronger model; because exact coverage is already available by concentration without that restriction, this lane is dropped.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The M17 lane records its named symmetry obstruction rather than mislabeling a concentration band as conformal inference.

seed_details.opened_evidence: The CCK generic construction calibrates a supremum through Gaussian approximation and anti-concentration, while Armstrong and Kolesar certify scalar finite-sample coverage by worst-case bias. Neither paper gives an exact conditional union bound over the finitely many random disk-count patterns generated by a flat boundary design.
seed_details.kernel: Construct an explicit count-selected finite-pattern band with nonasymptotic simultaneous coverage over every declared nonempty thickness-profile union and prove a matching expected-maximum-width lower bound on the pervasive class.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Enumerate disk intersection patterns by a three-dimensional affine arrangement and calibrate every selectable average conditional on the scores before bandwidth selection.
seed_details.target_method_search: No finite-sample sparse-cell boundary band with a matching pervasive all-band width converse was found.
adjacent_threads: Bull2012HonestAdaptiveBands: testing obstruction for adaptive band width
seed_details.red_team: This is a conservative VC union bound and cannot be a contribution beside modern multiplier bands.
seed_details.rebuttal: Its value is exact coverage under empty and polynomially sparse cells plus a same-class width lower bound; it is retained only as part of the full thickness-multiplicity frontier, not as a standalone calibration novelty.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The finite-pattern enumeration is paired with a matching all-band obstruction and is not sold as a generic replacement for multiplier bootstrap.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Gaiffas's Theorem 2 treats a single \(\Gamma\)-varying design zero and obtains a slowly varying pointwise minimax rate from the same bias--information equation used in the polynomial case.
seed_details.kernel: Derive isolated-versus-pervasive expected-sup and band-width frontiers for exponentially vanishing one-sided boundary mass, with explicit normalized flat laws.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Invert the severe tube-mass equation and then determine whether packing entropy enters inside or outside the slowly varying inverse.
seed_details.target_method_search: No boundary-uniform severe-thinning result with multiplicity profiles was located.
adjacent_threads: AntoniadisPenskySapatinas2014DensityZeros: finitely many inhomogeneities under global loss
seed_details.red_team: This follows mechanically by replacing powers with \(\Gamma\)-varying functions in the polynomial proof.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection is unresolved because severe inversion can change how the entropy term propagates; the candidate remains credible but lacks the explicit witness calculations available for the polynomial kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is retained only if it derives the severe inverse and same-class lower realization rather than extrapolating exponents.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Gaiffas's 2005 Introduction, Theorem 1, local-polynomial construction, and localized Gaussian proof establish the single-point information equation. The adjacent 2007 paper's Introduction, oracle equation, upper theorem, and localized lower theorem build a design-adaptive spatial normalization for finitely many polynomial density zeros, but do not select between boundary thin-site multiplicity regimes under unweighted global loss.
seed_details.kernel: Construct one estimator, independent of \(\kappa\) and the profile class, satisfying an oracle inequality that attains the isolated no-log rate when severity layers are sparse and the pervasive logarithmic rate when they are dense.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Estimate a location-and-severity entropy penalty from score counts and prove it does not retain the global \(\log n\) term on isolated profiles.
seed_details.target_method_search: Design-adaptive spatial rates exist for finitely many one-dimensional zeros, but no profile-adaptive boundary estimator with a same-loss isolated/pervasive oracle inequality was found.
seed_details.red_team: Gaiffas's spatially normalized adaptive estimator already removes local penalties near isolated zeros.
seed_details.rebuttal: His loss is normalized by a location-specific rate and assumes finitely many zeros; the requested estimator must adapt under one unweighted boundary supremum loss to an unknown multiplicity profile.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A global-rate estimator that always pays \(\log n\) would not satisfy this seed.
